intro: The CRC32 Checksum tool computes the CRC32 hash of any text you paste, encoding the input as UTF-8 bytes and applying the standard IEEE polynomial (0xEDB88320). It returns the 32-bit result as both an 8-digit zero-padded hexadecimal value and a decimal number. This is handy for quickly verifying data integrity, comparing strings, or generating short, deterministic checksums.
useCases: Verify that a string matches an expected CRC32 value reported by another tool or library
Generate a compact, deterministic checksum to use as a cache key or bucket identifier
Detect accidental changes by comparing the CRC32 of two text snippets
Reproduce the same CRC32 (IEEE) values used in zlib, PNG, and ZIP formats for short text inputs
Debug checksum mismatches by inspecting both the hex and decimal representations

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The CRC32 is computed entirely in your browser using JavaScript, and nothing you type is uploaded or stored on any server.

faq.q: Which CRC32 variant does this tool use?
faq.a: It uses the standard CRC-32/IEEE algorithm with the reversed polynomial 0xEDB88320, the same variant used by zlib, PNG, and ZIP. The result matches those implementations for identical byte input.

faq.q: How is the input encoded before hashing?
faq.a: The text is encoded as UTF-8 bytes before the checksum is computed. Non-ASCII characters are therefore hashed as their multi-byte UTF-8 representation.

faq.q: What format is the output in?
faq.a: It shows two lines: the checksum as an 8-character zero-padded lowercase hexadecimal value, and the same value in decimal.

faq.q: Is CRC32 suitable for security or cryptographic use?
faq.a: No. CRC32 is an error-detection checksum, not a cryptographic hash. Use it for integrity checks and quick comparisons, not for hashing passwords or signing data.
